## Learning objectives

By the end of this lab you will be able to:

- Model the technical truth of a real system before creating any metaphor.
- Design an isomorphic metaphor with an explicit technical-to-narrative mapping.
- Cast system responsibilities as characters with distinct voices.
- Break an explanation into scenes, each with an educational outcome.
- Write an audio-first, scene-oriented screenplay that is renderer-independent.
- Produce a 2–5 minute educational audio drama with a generative AI workflow.
- Evaluate the result across technical accuracy, metaphor quality, narrative
  clarity, audio communication, and learning outcome — with technical accuracy
  weighted highest.

## Lab method

This is a **substantial, judgement-building lab**. It follows the Open
Engineering Lab Method, mapped to the story pipeline:

```
OBSERVE      Understand the technical system.
INVESTIGATE  Identify actors, responsibilities, and relationships.
DESIGN       Create the metaphor and narrative mapping.
COMPOSE      Create characters, scenes, and screenplay.
EXECUTE      Generate the audio production.
EVALUATE     Review technical, educational, and audio quality.
REFLECT      Document what the metaphor clarified and what it obscured.
```

## Prerequisites

- Completion of the eight course modules (or equivalent familiarity).
- A text editor.
- A generative audio-production account (e.g. Wondercraft) with multivoice and
  sound-effect support; a free tier may suffice but may add watermarks or
  limits.

## Environment

- Operating system: any
- Required tools: a text editor; a generative audio production service
- Estimated time: 2–4 hours
